name: MOSS-Image SFT ComfyUI
readme:
# MOSS-Image SFT ComfyUI

Four browser workflows: BF16 photography, INT8 with two LoRA slots, experimental latent img2img, and the official prompt-enhanced graph. The same image supports the separate Runpod Hub queue API.

## Deploy

Use one NVIDIA GPU with at least 24 GB VRAM and a CUDA 13.0-compatible host. Set your own MOSS_PASSWORD of at least 12 characters before starting; login user is moss and there is no default password. Prefer a Runpod Secret. Keep the image entry point and start command unchanged.

Open HTTP port 8188 for preparation progress and protected ComfyUI. The landing page links all four native workflows. For photography open /?template=photography-bf16&source=moss. Port 22 uses your Runpod SSH key.

First startup downloads and verifies 23.51 GB of public models; no Hugging Face token is required. Preparation is not instant. The template provides 40 GB container disk and a 60 GB volume at /workspace. Retain the volume to preserve models, edited workflows, inputs and outputs. MOSS_VOLUME_GB=60 must match the provisioned volume size; update it when resizing.

Application files are baked under /opt/moss, /opt/comfyui and /opt/venv. Mutable data is under /workspace/moss, so a workspace mount does not hide the application. Restarts reuse verified models and preserve edited workflows.

The gateway derives the standard Runpod public origin automatically. For a custom domain, set MOSS_PUBLIC_ORIGIN to its exact HTTP(S) origin, including a nondefault port if needed and no path.

## Verified release

Version 0.1.0 pins the tested image digest. Three core presets passed on a fresh GPU Pod and queue worker; the optional API LoRA slot, actual prompt-enhanced browser generation, four native workflow imports, authenticated HTTP/WebSocket transport and restart preservation passed. Checks establish execution and persistence, not an aesthetic-quality guarantee.

README, API inputs, validation and upstream licenses: https://github.com/akhilsivanand/moss-runpod
